chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
When you send a falcon, or a hawk, or an eagle (to hunt), do not eat until you reach it and slaughter it. And if it has killed (the prey), do not eat.

key_terms.بَاز: Falcon (baz) — a trained falcon used for hunting
key_terms.تُذَكِّيَهُ: Tadhkiyah — ritual slaughter; purifying/making lawful by slaughtering according to Islamic rites
key_terms.عُقَاب: Eagle ('uqab) — a large bird of prey used in falconry

ai.seo_question: Is the prey caught by a falcon or hawk permissible to eat in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that game caught by birds of prey — specifically falcons, hawks, and eagles — is not permissible to eat unless the hunter reaches the prey while it is still alive and performs the ritual slaughter (tadhkiyah). This ruling addresses the common practice of falconry in early Islamic Arabia. If the bird of prey itself kills the game before the hunter can slaughter it, the meat is forbidden, distinguishing the Islamic requirement of ritual slaughter from mere capture by a trained bird.
